headline: Advance Boat Tour and Entry Pass Verification
reservation: While park entry is managed via the Discovery Pass, the Western Brook Pond boat tour requires separate advanced booking through private operators as it frequently sells out months in advance. Campsite and backcountry hut reservations are managed via the Parks Canada national system and should be confirmed prior to arrival in the region.

days.title: The Earth's Mantle and Coastal Cliffs

stops.name: The Tablelands
stops.detail: Walk upon exposed peridotite rock from the Earth's mantle, a geological rarity that defines the park's UNESCO status.

stops.name: Green Point
stops.detail: Examine the coastal cliffs featuring significant fossil records and unique geological folding.

days.driving: Allow 1 to 1.5 hours across the south and north arms; conditions vary
days.note: Wind speeds on the Tablelands can be significant; prepare for high exposure.

days.title: Fjords and Forested Valleys

stops.name: Western Brook Pond
stops.detail: Hike the flat boardwalk to reach the dock for a boat tour of the massive, land-locked fjord.

stops.name: Broom Point
stops.detail: Visit the restored fishing premises to learn about the traditional maritime heritage of the Gulf of St. Lawrence.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for transit between northern attractions; conditions vary
days.note: The walk to the Western Brook Pond dock takes approximately 45 minutes each way.

days.title: Summit Views and Harbour Life

stops.name: Gros Morne Mountain
stops.detail: Embark on a challenging trek to the park's highest point for a panoramic view of the Long Range Mountains.

stops.name: Lobster Cove Head Lighthouse
stops.detail: Explore the historic lighthouse grounds and scan the coastal waters for whale activity.

days.driving: Allow 30 to 45 minutes for local transfers; conditions vary
days.note: The mountain trail is seasonally closed in late spring to protect nesting ptarmigan and caribou.

intel.title: Western Brook Trailhead
intel.text: The main lot for Western Brook Pond is large but fills quickly before scheduled boat departures. Arrive well in advance of your tour time to ensure a spot.

intel.title: Rural Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in Rocky Harbour and Norris Point but fades quickly in the Tablelands and northern backcountry. Do not rely on digital maps for off-trail navigation.

intel.title: Community Pumps
intel.text: Fuel is available in Rocky Harbour and Deer Lake. Ensure you have sufficient supply before heading to the northernmost reaches near Cow Head.

intel.title: Seasonal Boat Access
intel.text: Boat tours typically operate from June through September. Water levels and wind conditions can occasionally lead to tour cancellations on short notice.

intel.title: Water Taxi Logistics
intel.text: Accessing the Bonne Bay trails often requires the seasonal water taxi between Woody Point and Norris Point. Check the local ferry schedule to avoid a long road detour.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Deer Lake Airport (YDF) and stop in Deer Lake for supplies before the drive to Rocky Harbour.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are sufficient for the main Viking Trail, but SUVs offer better comfort on secondary roads that may have seasonal frost heaves.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset at Lobster Cove Head Lighthouse provides an unobstructed view of the Gulf of St. Lawrence, subject to coastal fog.
